curriculum.lesson_evidence: A gymnastics sequence is a series of movements joined together with smooth links. A good sequence has a clear start shape, a middle (a balance, a roll or a jump) and a held finish pose. Changing level, speed and direction makes it interesting. Perform it on a mat with controlled movements and practise until it feels smooth. Offer easier options, such as walking instead of jumping.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Add a link and a finish to this sequence: a balance on one foot, then a low jump. Describe each.

FEEDBACK
Link: step smoothly from the balance into the jump with bent knees. Finish: land softly and hold a tall pose for 2 seconds. A clear finish shows control.

WATCH FOR
Thinking a sequence is just a list of tricks. Smooth links and held shapes make a sequence.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Compose a four-part gymnastics sequence with a start, a balance, a travel and a finish. Write cue words for each, practise five times, record a control score from 1 to 3 for each part and perform it for family. Give an easier option for each part.

Write a short reflection naming one choice you changed and why. Any movement is optional, adult-supervised and can be done in a gentler way or described instead.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Example four-part sequence. 1 Start: tall stretch, hold 2 seconds. 2 Balance: stork stand on one foot for 3 seconds. 3 Travel: two low jumps with soft landings. 4 Finish: egg roll, then rise to a tall pose. Links: slow and smooth. Marking: start shape, balance, landing and finish all held.

TRY FIRST
Add a link and a finish to this sequence: a balance on one foot, then a low jump. Describe each.

FEEDBACK
Link: step smoothly from the balance into the jump with bent knees. Finish: land softly and hold a tall pose for 2 seconds. A clear finish shows control.
teach_steps.explain:
A gymnastics sequence is a series of movements joined together with smooth links. A good sequence has a clear start shape, a middle (a balance, a roll or a jump) and a held finish pose. Changing level, speed and direction makes it interesting. Perform it on a mat with controlled movements and practise until it feels smooth. Offer easier options, such as walking instead of jumping.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make safe, healthy and respectful choices using clear cues and reasons, rather than guessing or copying others. Every choice keeps bodies safe and includes everyone.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the cues, rules or choices that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. For any movement, use a clear space, ask an adult to be nearby, move at your own comfortable level and stop if anything hurts or feels unsafe. You may always choose a gentler version or only describe the movement. One deliberate, reasoned change is more useful than a longer answer.
